title: Decaffeinated Coffee, pre-lightened and pre-sweetened with sugar

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated Coffee, pre-lightened and pre-sweetened with sugar (5214) is a ground coffee from which almost all caffeine has been removed, then lightly roasted and sweetened with sugar for a smoother taste. Ideal for those who want the coffee aroma without the stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually performed with water or solvents while preserving most flavor compounds.
A light roast retains brighter fruity notes compared to a dark roast.
Adding sugar creates a sweeter beverage without artificial sweeteners.
Decaf coffee is often used in diets that limit caffeine intake.
The sugar helps balance the natural bitterness of coffee.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Even without caffeine, coffee retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Certain coffee compounds can boost metabolic rate even in decaf form.

items.title: May reduce risk of some diseases
items.content: Regular moderate consumption of decaf coffee is linked to lower risk of type 2 diabetes and liver disease.

items.title: Provides energy without stimulation
items.content: Sugar offers a quick energy source, while coffee aroma can improve mood.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee contains small amounts of vitamins B2 and B3, supporting nervous system health.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The added sugar can raise blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

items.title: Residual caffeine
items.content: Decaf coffee still contains trace amounts of caffeine, which may affect highly caffeine‑sensitive persons.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can increase stomach acidity, causing discomfort for those with gastritis or reflux.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place 1‑2 tsp of ground coffee into 180‑200 ml of hot (not boiling) water, let steep for 3‑4 minutes, then filter. Add milk, cream, or extra sweeteners to taste if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to preserve aroma and prevent oxidation.
